scientific_boundary: All diagnostics below use already-exposed economics-v1 development and failed-holdout evidence. They may motivate a separately preregistered development lineage but are not confirmatory and cannot repair or rescue economics-v1.

development_surface.interpretation: The entire low-degree-of-freedom development surface appeared profitable rather than only the selected point. The subsequent holdout collapse therefore indicates broad development optimism / distribution mismatch, not merely a one-grid-cell ranking accident.

diagnostic_findings: Very large model-implied conservative EV and shape-edge values were common even though realized ROI was strongly negative, so raw model-vs-market edge magnitude is not calibrated enough to be treated as a direct purchase signal on this evidence.
The v1 fixed odds cap of 100 left a long-odds-heavy portfolio: median selected decimal odds were 39.2 and the 75th percentile was 60.1.
V1 placed up to one ticket per market per race, creating multiple correlated exposures in the same race; v2 should test at-most-one-ticket-per-race as a variance-control hypothesis.
Because these findings are post-holdout diagnostics, every proposed correction must be treated as development-only until independently validated on new meetings.
v2_hypotheses_motivated_not_proven: Tighter maximum odds may reduce uncalibrated tail exposure.
Higher probability floors and stricter model-agreement constraints may reduce fragile model-only edge signals.
Fewer unordered markets and one total ticket per race may reduce correlated portfolio variance.
Development policy selection should prioritize meeting robustness before pooled ROI.
forbidden_inference: Do not claim that any v2 hypothesis is true because economics-v1 failed. Only a separately preregistered fresh untouched validation can promote a v2 policy.
